chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madaini, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding the food of the prisoner, and he said: 'Feeding him is a right upon the one who captures him, and even if he intends to kill him the next day, for it is befitting that he is fed, and given drink, and shaded, and treated with kindness, whether he is an infidel or not.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a prisoner in Islamic jurisprudence according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the principle of *rafq* (gentleness) in Islamic jurisprudence, establishing that feeding and caring for a prisoner is a mandatory right of the captive upon the captor, irrespective of the prisoner's faith or imminent execution. It highlights the ethical obligation to maintain human dignity even in the context of war or captivity, reflecting the Shia emphasis on justice and mercy in interpersonal dealings.
